blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, the ability to produce a clean, traceable tax calculation is not a technical skill — it is a trust-building discipline. When the finance leader tells the CEO that the effective tax rate will be 23.4% this year, the CEO needs to know that this number came from a process which, if audited tomorrow, would hold up without reconstruction. That confidence is built over years, through calculations that always land on the same shape.

Built on that confidence, every strategic conversation about tax becomes easier. Discussions about investment, pricing, acquisitions and restructurings all depend on a shared, trusted view of what the tax consequences actually are. If that view wobbles because last year's numbers had to be corrected twice, every subsequent conversation carries a small, silent discount.

Calculation discipline, done quietly for years, is the foundation on which senior tax credibility rests.

items.q: According to the text, what kind of skill is producing a clean tax calculation at senior level?
items.why: "it is not a technical skill — it is a trust-building discipline."

items.q: What must the CEO be able to assume about the effective tax rate figure?
options: That it was produced by an external auditor
That it would hold up if audited tomorrow without reconstruction
That it will fall next year
That it matches the statutory rate
items.why: "a process which, if audited tomorrow, would hold up without reconstruction."

items.q: What does the phrase "carries a small, silent discount" suggest about later conversations?
options: They are quietly trusted a little less
items.why: Inferência: cada correção passada corrói, sem alarde, a confiança nas conversas seguintes.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Consistency in calculation earns executive trust over time
A single flawless calculation matters more than years of discipline
Tax credibility rests on quiet, repeated reliability
Corrected numbers weaken future strategic discussions
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende que a confiança se constrói ao longo de anos, não num único acerto.

items.q: The passage suggests that strategic decisions on acquisitions and pricing depend on…
options: a shared, trusted view of the tax consequences
the lowest possible effective tax rate
the personal reputation of the CEO
items.why: "all depend on a shared, trusted view of what the tax consequences actually are."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily orientando o novo head of tax. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome aboard. Before you touch a single figure, I want you to understand why this desk has kept the CFO's trust for seven years. It isn't cleverness. It's that every calculation lands on the same shape, every time.

Here is the standard. Anything you hand up must be traceable — I should be able to walk any number back to its source in under a minute. It must be reviewed by a second pair of eyes before it leaves this room. And, most importantly, it must never be corrected twice. Correcting once is honest. Correcting the same figure a second time tells the CFO the process wobbled, and that impression is expensive to undo.

You'll be tempted to move faster than this allows. Resist that. A rate delivered a day late and defensible beats a rate delivered on time that you cannot reconstruct if someone challenges it.

Get this right, quietly, for a couple of years, and you'll find every strategic conversation — pricing, acquisitions, restructurings — starts from a place of trust rather than doubt.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily say the desk's seven years of trust is built on?
options: Calculations that land on the same shape every time
Delivering figures faster than any other team
items.why: "It isn't cleverness. It's that every calculation lands on the same shape, every time."

items.q: What does 'traceable' mean in Emily's standard?
options: The figures are stored for seven years
Any number can be walked back to its source quickly
The calculation is done by two people
Every number is signed by the CFO
items.why: "I should be able to walk any number back to its source in under a minute."

items.q: Why does Emily insist a figure must never be corrected twice?
options: A second correction signals to the CFO that the process wobbled
items.why: "Correcting the same figure a second time tells the CFO the process wobbled."

items.q: What does Emily imply the new head of tax will be tempted to do — and should avoid?
items.why: Inferência: ela avisa contra ir rápido demais e prefere um número defensável a um número entregue no prazo mas irreconstruível.

items.q: How would you best describe the underlying message of Emily's advice?
options: Reviews slow the team down unnecessarily
Quiet, consistent discipline earns trust that speed cannot
Trust is won through occasional brilliance
The CFO cares only about the final rate
items.why: Inferência: a fala inteira defende a disciplina discreta e repetida como base da credibilidade.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every figure we submit must be fully traceable." Traceable means…
options: able to be followed back to its source
items.why: Traceable = rastreável: dá para seguir o número de volta até a origem.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Our effective tax rate was 23.4%, well below the ___ rate of 34%."
items.why: A alíquota efetiva se contrasta com a alíquota legal (statutory).

items.q: "The model has to hold up under audit." To hold up here means to…
items.why: To hold up = sustentar-se, resistir ao exame sem cair por terra.

items.q: "When last year's figures had to be redone, confidence began to wobble." To wobble means to…
items.why: To wobble = oscilar, ficar instável — a confiança tremeu.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Years of clean work are the ___ on which senior tax credibility rests."
items.why: Foundation = fundação, a base sobre a qual a credibilidade se apoia.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas de finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO won't sign off on the rate until it's fully reconciled." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new calculation standard across all jurisdictions." To roll out means to…
options: implement in a planned, staged way
cancel one region at a time
items.why: Roll out = implantar de forma progressiva e planejada.

items.q: "The regional controller pushed back on the timing assumption." She…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They promised a cleaner process but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi prometido.

items.q: "Reconciling those two entries won't move the needle on the effective rate." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, causar diferença perceptível.
